cutSystemsNote: Resonance, Bleed, Anchors, Suppression and the five ground roles were cut on 2026-09-20 (open-questions.json: resonance-playability, bleed-playability, anchors-without-resonance, ground-roles-viability). Their blocks were removed from this file on 2026-09-25. Build nothing on them.

frameEconomy.hpAsCampaignResource: Frame HP is a campaign resource, not an encounter resource. Frames do not heal between fights. They move down a damage-state track: Operational -> Degraded -> Critical -> Hulked.

damageStateEffects.hulked: No actions; the machine is out of the fight.
damageStateEffects.note: Carried over on 2026-09-25 from the retired two-scale design (it was that document's §8, and design/ux-doctrine.md §3 still relies on it). Not re-confirmed since lockstep: open-questions.json#frame-damage-action-caps.

repair.cost: Repairing a step costs technician-days, drawn from a single shared weekly pool the Directorate allocates.
repair.sharedPoolNote: Frame modification/customization draws from the exact same pool. Repairing a friend's Frame and upgrading your own compete directly for the same finite resource — this is the primary economic tension of downtime.

upgradePoints.model: A credit budget that buys capability, never levels (settled 2026-09-20). Pilot and machine share one level and advance together on milestone XP. Credits buy the machine's own feats, weapons, armour and equipment: some consumable or renewable, some permanent with once-per-round, once-per-hour or once-per-day abilities.
upgradePoints.earnedFrom: Downtime activities, and winning fights at both personnel and Frame scale.
upgradePoints.pool: INDIVIDUAL per pilot, not shared. Deliberately unlike technician-days: each pilot has their own repair crew (see repairCrew below), so investing in your own Frame never means taking from a squadmate.
upgradePoints.acquisition: In-fiction requests to the quartermaster or the pilot's crew, read out of Foundry logs and answered with balanced options.
upgradePoints.overInvestmentCost: No new mechanic needed. Upgrade work spends discretionary slices, so slices spent in the hangar are slices not spent resting, and fatigue climbs. All work and no rest punishes itself.

repairCrew.confirmed: 2026-09-06. Each pilot has their own repair crew: standing NPCs, and the relationship carries real mechanical weight in both directions.
repairCrew.goodStanding: Treat them well and they go beyond the allocation. The user's own example: go out drinking with your repair crew and they might put in a night shift nobody asked them for.
repairCrew.neglected: A neglected crew provides less HP healing per repair.
repairCrew.whyItIsNotRedundantWithTechnicianDays: Two different axes. The technician-day pool is the Directorate's SHARED allocation — how much repair time you are granted, competed for between pilots. Crew standing is PERSONAL and scales how much you get OUT of that time. Allocation versus effectiveness.
repairCrew.namedChief: Confirmed 2026-09-09: each crew has one named head, six total (data/npcs/repair-chief-*.json, linked via npc.schema.json's crewChiefForRef). Currently placeholders — Ingram's own framing: 'six lesser NPCs who may grow into bigger more interesting roles later.'

floorAndBoost.principle: A crew is always working, whether or not the pilot shows up — 'repair crews are always working around the clock.' A guaranteed baseline HP repair happens automatically every technician-day cycle regardless of PC involvement (the floor). Direct PC involvement — showing up and working alongside the crew, not just spending the resource — restores substantially more HP than the floor alone, representing real labour, not a relationship-standing multiplier layered on top of it.

repairCrew.coversVehicles: Confirmed 2026-09-09: a pilot's repair crew maintains their vehicle as well as their Frame, drawing from the same technician-day allocation. Splitting a limited pool between Frame repair and vehicle repair is a real player choice, not two separate economies.

frameEconomy.deployability: Not all six Frames are necessarily deployable at once. A Degraded or Critical Frame may be riskier or unable to launch. When a Contact only calls for two or three Frames, the players choose the subset — the GM never has to force this; the repair economy does it for them.
frameEconomy.permanentLoss: A Frame that reaches Hulked can stay Hulked. Permanent loss of a personal Frame is on the table from the start (foreshadow it early, so when it happens it reads as the campaign keeping a promise, not GM cruelty). Confirmed 2026-09-09: this applies equally to vehicles; badly damaging or destroying one is acceptable and expected, and generates real repair backlog, same as a Frame. PC death is never the cost mechanism at either scale.
frameEconomy.supersededNote: UPDATED 2026-09-20: lockstep levelling and the credit budget (see upgradePoints). Frames and vehicles are PC-grade sheets that amplify the pilot (GitHub #196). See open-questions.json#frame-upgrade-economy, #levelling-and-request-fulfilment and #vehicle-and-frame-rules-model.

timeEconomy.slicesRevisionNote: Was 2, revised 2026-09-06 once the day gained a real four-quarter shape (morning/afternoon/evening/night) during UX design work — see design/ux-doctrine.md §3/§7a. One discretionary slice per quarter is now the intended granularity, not a smaller number spread across four.
timeEconomy.mandatoryLoad: School (morning + afternoon only) is a standing option, on offer most days like anything else. Choosing it still spends the quarter's slice, the same as any other pick. In practice it's the default most players take most days, which is what keeps a day feeling structured even though nothing forces the choice mechanically.
timeEconomy.designIntent: More options exist than slices to spend them on — that gap is the entire engine of downtime play.
timeEconomy.restIsAlwaysAvailable: Even a player with nothing else planned, or one running high on fatigue (see fatigue below), can always spend a quarter's slice resting instead. Encouraged, not just permitted.

options.name: Frame Modification
options.cost: 1+ slices, from the shared technician-day pool

options.name: Repair Advocacy
options.effect: Push a Frame back up the damage-state track.

options.name: Analysis Duty
options.effect: Read the sensor archive: reveals the current Contact Pool state, or pushes the floor back (delays the next possible Contact).

options.name: Rest
options.effect: Recover — confirmed 2026-09-06 to be a category of several named rest activities, each with a different SF2E-relevant bonus (e.g. a quiet option weighted toward HP recovery, hospital care targeting HP and debuffs, a social outing for a different kind of bonus). The specific roster and numbers are not yet designed.

fatigue.description: Working consecutive segments without resting triggers a check to see how tired the character is; the check gets harder each additional segment worked without a rest, and failing enough of them ends in involuntary unconsciousness and the loss of that segment's slot. Confirmed 2026-09-06 (design/ux-doctrine.md §3); grounded in but goes beyond PC2E's own flat "fatigued at 16 hours" rule (reference/srd/player-core/489-exploration-mode.json).
fatigue.resetBy: likely resting, exact mechanism not yet decided alongside the rest-activity-roster question

contactPool.activeFrom: Day 7 (the opening arc, Days 1-6, is hand-placed and does not roll).
contactPool.designIntent: Bounded on both ends by design: players are never punished with a zero-warning attack, and tension never gets an indefinite escape hatch either. Starting numbers below are a proposed baseline, not fixed — tune freely.

floor.description: No Contact can trigger within 2 quiet days of the last one. No roll happens during this window at all.

rollProcedure.description: Contact triggers on a 20. The target number drops by 1 for each additional quiet morning (20, then 19+, then 18+...) — visible, predictable, escalating.

ceiling.description: If Contact hasn't triggered by the 8th quiet morning (target would be 13+), it happens automatically. The pool can never coast forever.

contactPool.analysisDutyInteraction: Analysis Duty either reveals the current target number to the players, or spends a slice to push the floor back by a fixed number of days (a guaranteed delay). Either way, tactical certainty is purchased with personal time — the same currency as everything else in this game.

falseContact.sharedCost: All three types cost the same disrupted evening as a real Contact.

types.name: Genuine false positive
types.description: Full scramble, nothing there. Teaches players early that the cost of readiness isn't only the Claimants — the system itself has a price.

types.name: Role reversal
types.description: The scramble is real, but what needs help is people, not a fight. The Frames end up rescuing "children" (evacuees, civilians, possibly off-duty kids) rather than the other way around. Same adrenaline shape, subverted resolution.

types.name: First contact with the Watcher
types.description: A false or ambiguous response that is actually the first evidence of a second, invisible antagonist. Doesn't resolve as combat — resolves as an investigation hook, and shouldn't be closed out quickly.
